doc.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Keeping her orchestra together
summary: The band has mutual respect and long Monday-night history; the difficulty is logistics.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Marvelous. Wow. You gave me a lot of food for thought here. Excellent. Is it, from a logistical standpoint, difficult to keep a band together these days?

Well not really. You know I think it would be difficult except that thankfully my whole group there’s a mutual respect in the group, to me, to each other, hopefully they feel that from me. And when you have that respect for each other, everybody’s feeling respected by each other and you want to be in that situation. So when we come together immediately there is this good feeling. And everybody sits down to play, because we played this gig for five years every Monday night in New York when Bizioni’s was around. It’s kind of like putting on an old glove. It’s been difficult for me just time wise,
